subject.title: v2026.6.8: plugin_state_entries SQLite database corruption — session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released

question: Should OpenClaw prioritize availability-first shared SQLite corruption recovery for `openclaw.sqlite`, or require stronger proof of the session-takeover-to-corruption cause before changing shared-state behavior?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the correct behavior changes data retention, recovery, WAL/checkpoint, and session-lock policy for a persisted store used by many runtime surfaces.

options.title: Define shared-state recovery first
options.body: Choose a quarantine/preserve/fresh-state policy for malformed `openclaw.sqlite`, then implement focused plugin-state and task-state recovery proof.

options.title: Prove corruption cause first
options.body: Keep fail-closed behavior while maintainers collect preserved database sidecars, integrity traces, and a live takeover-to-corruption reproduction.

options.title: Split recovery and lock work
options.body: Track shared SQLite recovery separately from open session-lock issues, and close this only after both halves have canonical owners.

recommendation.title: Define shared-state recovery first
recommendation.body: Choose a quarantine/preserve/fresh-state policy for malformed `openclaw.sqlite`, then implement focused plugin-state and task-state recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest ownership signal is the database-first refactor that introduced shared SQLite as the runtime state boundary.
